Why does a provincial legislature grant engineers the right to regulate themselves? A. To limit competition from engineers trained abroad B. To raise the income of qualified engineers C. To reduce the cost of government D. To protect the public by having qualified people set and enforce standards Self-regulation is a bargain: exclusive rights to title and practice are granted so the profession protects the public. Benefits to members are side effects, not the purpose.

entries.h: Practice question I-02: Right to title
entries.x: A new chemical engineering graduate has not yet applied to any regulator. Which title may she use on her business card? A. Bachelor of Applied Science in Chemical Engineering B. Engineer-in-Training C. P.Eng. (pending) D. Chemical Engineer Until she is registered with a regulator, she may not use 'engineer', 'EIT' or 'P.Eng.' in any form. Stating her degree is factual and allowed.

entries.h: Practice question I-03: Scope of practice
entries.x: Which activity most clearly falls within the reserved practice of professional engineering? A. Selling engineering software to a client B. Running a standard laboratory test by following a written procedure C. Designing the relief system for a pressure vessel in a public facility D. Drafting a drawing under instruction, with no design decisions Reserved practice needs both the application of engineering principles and something to safeguard (life, health, property, environment). Relief-system design has both.

Why do engineering regulators' councils include public (lay) members? A. To provide legal advice to council B. To bring an outside, public-interest perspective to regulation C. To manage the regulator's finances D. To represent engineering employers Public members are not registrants. They add a public viewpoint and accountability to a self-regulating body.

Which organization accredits undergraduate engineering programs in Canada? A. The Canadian Society for Chemical Engineering B. The Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board of Engineers Canada C. The Standards Council of Canada D. The provincial regulator in each province Engineers Canada accredits programs through the CEAB. It does not license or discipline individuals; provincial regulators do.

entries.h: Practice question I-06: Attributes of a profession
entries.x: Which feature distinguishes a profession from other skilled occupations? A. Its members belong to a union B. Its members earn high salaries C. It is self-regulated under statute and committed to serving the public D. It requires a university degree Many occupations need degrees or pay well. A profession combines specialized knowledge with statutory self-regulation and a primary duty to the public.

entries.h: Practice question II-01: Codes of ethics
entries.x: In Canadian engineering codes of ethics, which duty is paramount? A. Duty to the safety, health and welfare of the public and the environment B. Duty to the employer C. Duty to the profession D. Duty to the client Every code puts public safety, health and welfare (now with the environment) first and makes all other duties subordinate when it is at stake.

An engineer argues that a new highway is right because it benefits the largest number of people, even though a few residents lose their homes. Which theory is this? A. Utilitarianism B. Rights ethics C. Duty ethics D. Virtue ethics Weighing total benefits against harms to choose the greatest good for the greatest number is utilitarian (Mill). Rights ethics would focus on the displaced residents' rights.

Which theory holds that the right action is a 'golden mean' between two extremes? A. Aristotle's virtue ethics B. Mill's utilitarianism C. Kant's duty ethics D. Locke's rights ethics Aristotle's virtue ethics describes virtues such as courage as a mean between excess and deficiency.

A weakness most often attributed to duty (Kantian) ethics is that it: A. Depends entirely on cultural custom B. Can justify harming a minority for the majority's benefit C. Ignores the consequences of actions and offers no way to resolve conflicting duties D. Is too vague to apply Duty ethics judges acts by the rule followed, not outcomes, and gives little help when two duties clash. Harming a minority is the classic criticism of utilitarianism.

entries.h: Practice question II-05: Conflict of interest
entries.x: An engineer owns shares in a pump manufacturer and is asked by a client to recommend pump suppliers. What should the engineer do first? A. Sell the shares secretly and then recommend the manufacturer B. Refuse to work for the client ever again C. Recommend the manufacturer, since its pumps are good D. Disclose the shareholding to the client in writing before advising Disclosure lets the client give informed consent or choose another adviser. If the interest could corrupt the advice, the engineer should step aside or divest.

entries.h: Practice question II-06: Conflict of interest
entries.x: Which situation is a conflict of interest even if the engineer acts with complete honesty? A. Working overtime on a project B. Using a well-known design code C. Recommending the lowest-cost compliant bidder D. Reviewing, for a municipality, a design prepared by the engineer's own firm A perceived conflict damages trust even when judgment is sound. Reviewing your own firm's work for a regulator is a classic actual-or-perceived conflict.

Management rejects an engineer's recommendation to use a more expensive coating. There is no safety or environmental risk either way. What should the engineer do? A. Report management to the regulator B. Resign in protest C. Use the expensive coating anyway D. Document the recommendation and its consequences, then accept the decision Where public safety is not at stake, the employer may make business decisions. The engineer's duty is to explain the consequences clearly, preferably in writing.

A contractor whose change-order claims you assess offers you a weekend at a ski resort. You should: A. Accept, and approve only half of the claims to show impartiality B. Accept, because it does not affect your judgment C. Decline the offer D. Accept, but disclose it afterwards Accepting a significant gift from a party whose claims you judge creates a conflict and the appearance of bias. Decline it.

entries.h: Practice question II-09: Reviewing another engineer's work
entries.x: A client asks you to review drawings prepared by another engineer who is still engaged on the project. Ethically, you should: A. Review them without telling anyone B. Notify the other engineer that you have been asked to review the work C. Offer to take over the project at a lower fee D. Refuse, because reviewing another engineer's work is never allowed Codes require courtesy and fairness to colleagues: inform the engineer whose work you review (unless their engagement has ended). Undercutting to supplant them is unethical.

entries.h: Practice question II-10: Confidentiality vs safety
entries.x: During an assignment you learn from confidential client data that a structure open to the public is at risk of collapse. The client asks you to keep quiet. You should: A. Urge the client to act, and if it will not, report to the appropriate authority B. Resign and say nothing C. Keep the information confidential as the client asks D. Tell the media immediately Public safety overrides confidentiality. Give the client the chance to act first; if it refuses, report to the authority. Going to the media first, or staying silent, are both wrong.

Under what conditions may an employed engineer do private consulting in the evenings? A. Whenever the work is outside office hours B. Never; moonlighting always breaches the code C. When the employer knows, no employer resources or confidential information are used, and there is no competition with the employer D. Only if the client is a relative Moonlighting is acceptable with disclosure and without using the employer's time, equipment, confidential information or competing with it.

In a structured ethical decision process, what should come immediately after identifying the ethical problem? A. Reporting the issue to the regulator B. Implementing the first acceptable solution C. Generating alternative courses of action D. Seeking legal advice in every case Identify the issue, generate alternatives, evaluate them against law, code and theories, then decide and act. Scenarios often hide a third, better option.

entries.h: Practice question III-01: Standard of care
entries.x: The standard of care expected of a professional engineer is that of: A. A reasonably competent engineer in the same field and circumstances B. Perfection: no errors are permitted C. An average member of the public D. The leading expert in the country Courts judge professionals against a reasonably competent practitioner in the same discipline and circumstances at that time, not against perfection or the top expert.

When may an engineer seal drawings that she did not personally prepare? A. Never B. When they were prepared under her direct supervision, or she reviewed them thoroughly and accepts responsibility for them C. When her manager instructs her to D. When the drafting technician has more experience than she does A seal is acceptance of professional responsibility. It may go only on work prepared under the engineer's supervision or fully reviewed, and within her competence.

Applying a professional seal to a report means that the engineer: A. Transfers liability to the employer B. Guarantees the report is free of errors C. Accepts professional responsibility for the work in it D. Certifies the client's compliance with the law The seal shows who takes responsibility. It is not a warranty or a guarantee of perfection.

Which document should normally not be sealed? A. A draft report marked 'Preliminary, not for construction' B. A final design drawing issued for construction C. A final geotechnical report issued to a municipality D. A specification issued for tender Final documents issued for use by others are sealed. Drafts are marked preliminary instead, so nobody relies on them as final.

A client buys insurance and signs a fixed-price contract to deal with cost-overrun risk. Which risk response is this? A. Mitigation B. Transfer C. Avoidance D. Acceptance Insurance and fixed-price contracts shift the financial consequence to another party: risk transfer. Mitigation would reduce the likelihood or the impact itself.

In a qualitative risk assessment, each risk is usually ranked on which two dimensions? A. Cost and schedule B. Owner and contractor C. Probability of occurrence and severity of consequence D. Detectability and frequency of inspection A risk matrix ranks likelihood against consequence. Some methods add detectability (as in FMEA), but the core pair is probability and severity.

Which control sits highest in the hierarchy of hazard controls? A. Warning signs and training B. Personal protective equipment C. Eliminating the hazard D. Engineering controls such as guards Elimination comes first, then substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls and finally PPE.

Professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance for engineers is usually written on a claims-made basis. What does that mean? A. It covers only claims made during the construction period B. It pays only if the client makes the claim, not a third party C. It covers claims first made while the policy is in force, so cover is needed after the engineer stops practising D. It covers bodily injury caused by the engineer's car A claims-made policy responds to claims made during the policy period, regardless of when the work was done. Retiring engineers need run-off (tail) cover.

Which policy is designed to cover a firm against third-party bodily injury and property damage from its operations, but not professional negligence? A. Directors and officers insurance B. Commercial general liability insurance C. Professional liability insurance D. A performance bond CGL covers bodily injury and property damage claims from operations and typically excludes professional services.

A contractor goes bankrupt halfway through a project. Which instrument protects the owner's cost to complete the work? A. Labour and material payment bond B. Certificate of insurance C. Bid bond D. Performance bond A surety's performance bond guarantees completion of the contract. A payment bond protects unpaid subcontractors and suppliers; a bid bond protects against a bidder refusing to sign.

An engineer acting as a site supervisor is charged with an OH&S offence. Which defence is most likely to succeed? A. The engineer did not intend the accident B. Due diligence: proof that every reasonable precaution was taken C. The regulation was not posted on site D. The worker was a subcontractor's employee Most OH&S offences are strict liability. Lack of intent is no defence, but proving due diligence on a balance of probabilities is.

What is the legal status of the National Building Code of Canada on its own? A. It has no legal force until a province, territory or municipality adopts it B. It binds only federal buildings C. It is federal law that applies across Canada D. It overrides provincial building codes The NBC is a model code. It becomes law only when adopted, with or without amendments, by a jurisdiction such as a province.

An engineer uses commercial finite-element software for a design. Who is responsible for the correctness of the results used in the design? A. The engineer who uses and relies on the results B. The software vendor C. Nobody, if the software is widely used D. The client who paid for the licence The professional must understand the software's limits, validate results with independent checks and remains accountable for the design.

An engineer believes her company is releasing effluent above its permit limits. What should she normally do first? A. Verify the facts and raise the issue internally, in writing B. Contact a newspaper C. Resign immediately D. Post the evidence on social media Unless harm is imminent, check the facts and use internal routes first. Report to the regulator or authority if the company does not act.

Sustainable development is best defined as development that: A. Has no environmental impact B. Maximizes economic growth C. Meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own D. Uses only renewable energy This is the Brundtland Commission definition (1987) used throughout Canadian engineering guidelines.

Which standard sets requirements for an environmental management system? A. ISO 9001 B. CSA Z662 C. ISO 14001 D. ISO 45001 ISO 14001 is environmental management; ISO 9001 is quality management; ISO 45001 is occupational health and safety. CSA Z662 covers oil and gas pipeline systems.

An engineer-in-training prepares calculations for a design. Who is professionally responsible for them? A. The client B. The professional engineer who supervises, reviews and seals the work C. The EIT alone D. The firm's accountant Trainees may practise only under the direct supervision of a registrant, who takes responsibility for the work by reviewing and sealing it.

What is the standard of proof in a civil lawsuit for negligence? A. Beyond a reasonable doubt B. Clear and convincing evidence C. Absolute certainty D. Balance of probabilities Civil claims are decided on a balance of probabilities (more likely than not). Beyond a reasonable doubt is the criminal standard.

Which is an essential element of an enforceable contract? A. A witness to the signatures B. Consideration flowing between the parties C. Registration with a court D. A written document signed by both parties The elements are offer and acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relations, capacity and legality. Most contracts need not be written.

entries.h: Practice question IV-03: Offer and acceptance
entries.x: A contractor mails a bid to an owner on 1 March. The owner receives it on 4 March. When is the bid effective? A. When the bid closing time passes B. When the owner awards the contract C. 4 March, when it is received D. 1 March, under the postal acceptance rule A bid is an offer, and offers are effective on receipt. The postal rule applies only to acceptances.

Under the Contract A / Contract B framework, when does Contract A arise? A. When the owner publishes the call for tenders B. When a bidder submits a compliant bid C. When the owner awards the construction contract D. When construction starts Ron Engineering (1981): a compliant bid creates Contract A, typically making the bid irrevocable during its validity period. Contract B is the construction contract formed on award.

Tender documents state that 'the lowest or any tender will not necessarily be accepted.' Can the owner accept the lowest bid even though it is non-compliant? A. No, the privilege clause does not permit accepting a non-compliant bid B. Only if the other bidders agree C. Yes, the privilege clause allows any choice D. Yes, if the bid is the cheapest M.J.B. Enterprises (1999): the owner owes compliant bidders an implied duty not to accept a non-compliant bid, despite a privilege clause.

A clause in a contract drafted by the owner is ambiguous. A court will usually interpret it: A. By asking an engineer to decide B. Against the owner, who drafted it C. In favour of the owner D. By ignoring the clause Contra proferentem: ambiguity is resolved against the party who drafted the clause.

After signing a contract, a flood unforeseen by either party makes performance impossible. Which doctrine applies? A. Quantum meruit B. Frustration C. Repudiation D. Promissory estoppel Frustration ends a contract when an unforeseen event, not caused by either party, makes performance impossible or radically different. A force majeure clause may deal with the same event expressly.

A supplier delivers a heat exchanger late. The owner's plant could not start, and the owner claims lost profits. Which principle limits the damages the owner can recover? A. The owner can recover all losses, however remote B. Only punitive damages are available C. The losses must have been within the parties' reasonable contemplation when they contracted D. Damages are always limited to the contract price Under Hadley v. Baxendale, recoverable losses are those arising naturally from the breach or within the parties' contemplation. The owner must also mitigate.

A consultant performs extra work at the client's request but no price was ever agreed. On what basis can the consultant recover payment? A. Specific performance B. Quantum meruit C. Liquidated damages D. Rescission Quantum meruit allows recovery of the reasonable value of work done where no enforceable price or contract exists.

An engineer tries to assign her personal obligations under a professional services contract to a colleague without the client's consent. The result is most likely that: A. The assignment of the obligations is not effective without the client's consent B. The contract becomes void for both parties C. The client must accept the colleague D. The assignment is valid because all contracts are assignable Rights to payment can generally be assigned, but obligations to perform personal professional services cannot be transferred without the other party's consent.

Which list states what a plaintiff must prove in a negligence action against an engineer? A. Duty of care, breach of the standard of care, causation and damage B. Fault and criminal intent C. A signed contract and a breach D. Intent, breach and damage Negligence requires a duty of care, a breach of the standard, causation (including foreseeable, not too remote, harm) and actual damage. No contract or intent is needed.

An engineering firm prepares tender drawings for a highway owner. A contractor relies on them in its bid and loses money because they are wrong. Can the contractor sue the engineering firm even though they had no contract? A. No, because engineers can only be sued by their clients B. Yes, in negligence, because reliance by bidders was foreseeable C. Only if the owner agrees D. No, because of privity of contract Edgeworth Construction v. N.D. Lea (1993): the firm owed a duty of care to contractors who foreseeably relied on its tender documents. Privity limits contract claims, not tort claims.

Two contractors' separate negligence caused one flood. Under joint and several liability, the plaintiff: A. Can recover only half from each B. Can recover twice the damages C. Must sue both together or recover nothing D. Can recover the full damages from either contractor Each joint tortfeasor can be made to pay the whole loss; they then sort out contribution between themselves.

An employee of an engineering firm makes a negligent error while doing her assigned work. Who can be held liable? A. Only the employee B. Only the firm C. Neither, because it was an honest mistake D. The firm vicariously, and the employee personally Employers are vicariously liable for employees' torts in the course of employment, and the employee remains personally liable for her own negligence.

A Canadian firm has a valuable, unpatented manufacturing process that competitors cannot see. Which protection best suits it? A. A trademark B. Industrial design registration C. Copyright registration D. Trade secret protection, backed by confidentiality measures A secret process can be protected indefinitely as a trade secret if the firm takes reasonable steps to keep it confidential. Copyright protects expression, not processes.

Which is the term of a Canadian patent? A. Life of the inventor plus 70 years B. 15 years from publication C. 20 years from the filing date, subject to maintenance fees D. 10 years from grant, renewable Canadian patents last up to 20 years from filing, if annual maintenance fees are paid.

An inventor presents her new catalyst at a conference before filing a patent application. What is the effect in Canada? A. She can never obtain a patent anywhere B. The disclosure has no effect on patentability C. She has 12 months from her disclosure to file in Canada, but may lose rights in countries without a grace period D. She must file within 30 days Canada (like the US) gives a 12-month grace period for the applicant's own disclosure. Many countries, including in Europe, give none.

A consulting engineer, working as an independent contractor without a written agreement, prepares calculation software for a client. Who owns the copyright? A. The regulator B. The consulting engineer C. It is in the public domain D. The client, because it paid Absent an agreement, the author owns copyright. The employer-ownership rule applies to employees, not independent contractors.

An engineer retained as an expert witness by the plaintiff owes her primary duty to: A. The plaintiff who pays her B. The plaintiff's lawyer C. Her employer D. The court An expert's overriding duty is to assist the court impartially (White Burgess, 2015). A contingency fee would compromise that independence.

What is the main purpose of the holdback required by construction lien legislation? A. To pay the consultant's fees B. To pay the owner's legal costs C. To create a fund from which valid lien claims of subcontractors and suppliers can be paid D. To penalize late contractors Holdbacks (typically 10 %) limit the owner's lien exposure and ensure money is available for those down the payment chain.

Which statement about workers' compensation in Canada is correct? A. Workers must prove the employer was at fault to receive benefits B. It applies only to unionized workers C. It is no-fault insurance, and in exchange workers generally cannot sue their employer D. It is a federal program administered by the Canada Revenue Agency Provincial workers' compensation pays benefits regardless of fault and bars most lawsuits against employers.

Which is one of the three basic rights of workers under Canadian OH&S legislation? A. The right to refuse unsafe work without reprisal B. The right to a pay increase after an accident C. The right to choose their supervisor D. The right to inspect the employer's financial records Workers have the right to know about hazards, to participate in health and safety, and to refuse unsafe work.

An employer requires all field engineers to pass a demanding fitness test. When is this requirement lawful despite its discriminatory effect? A. Never B. When it is a bona fide occupational requirement and accommodation is impossible without undue hardship C. Only if the union agrees D. Whenever the employer believes it is useful Under the Meiorin test, a standard must be rationally connected to the job, adopted in good faith and reasonably necessary, with accommodation to the point of undue hardship.

What can a mediator do that an arbitrator normally does not? A. Hear sworn evidence B. Meet privately with each party to explore settlement C. Award costs D. Impose a binding decision Mediators facilitate a voluntary settlement and often caucus with each side. Arbitrators hear evidence and make a binding award.

entries.h: Practice question IV-25: Quebec civil law
entries.x: Which statement about law in Quebec is correct? A. Quebec uses English common law for contracts B. Quebec's criminal law differs from the rest of Canada C. Patent law does not apply in Quebec D. Quebec's private law is based on the Civil Code of Quebec, while federal laws such as the Criminal Code apply as elsewhere Quebec's private law (contracts, property, liability) is codified in the Civil Code; federal law, including criminal and patent law, is the same across Canada.

entries.h: Practice question V-01: Act, regulations, bylaws
entries.x: Which instrument ranks highest in the legal framework of an engineering regulator? A. The Act passed by the legislature B. The regulator's bylaws C. The council's policies D. The regulator's practice guidelines The Act is the statute. Regulations and bylaws are made under it and cannot conflict with it.

A person who is not registered keeps practising engineering after warnings from the regulator. Which remedy can stop the ongoing practice? A. A practice review B. A reprimand from council C. A disciplinary hearing D. An injunction from a superior court Discipline applies only to registrants. Against non-registrants the regulator uses enforcement: prosecution for an offence and an injunction to restrain continued practice.

entries.h: Practice question V-03: Misuse of title
entries.x: Which is most likely to be misuse of a protected title? A. A P.Eng. signing letters as 'P.Eng.' B. An EIT registered with the regulator using 'EIT' C. A graduate describing her B.Eng. degree on a CV D. An unregistered person advertising services as 'Professional Engineer' Using 'Professional Engineer' or 'P.Eng.' without registration is holding out, an offence even if no engineering is performed.

Which requirement is common to all Canadian engineering regulators for professional registration? A. Membership in a technical society B. Demonstrating good character C. A graduate degree D. Canadian citizenship All regulators assess good character, along with academic qualifications, experience, professional practice knowledge and language. Citizenship and society membership are not required.

How does a technical society differ from a regulator? A. A technical society disciplines members for breaches of the code B. There is no difference C. A technical society licenses engineers in specialized fields D. A technical society advances technical knowledge; it does not regulate practice Regulators are statutory bodies that license and discipline to protect the public. Societies are voluntary bodies that share technical knowledge.

What standard of proof applies in a professional discipline hearing in Canada? A. Beyond a reasonable doubt B. Prima facie evidence only C. The registrant must prove innocence D. Balance of probabilities Discipline is a civil-type proceeding: the regulator must prove its case on a balance of probabilities, with clear and cogent evidence.

Which conduct is most likely to lead to disciplinary action? A. Declining an assignment outside one's competence B. Charging a fee higher than a competitor's C. Joining a technical society D. Sealing drawings for a type of project outside one's demonstrated competence Practising and sealing outside one's competence breaches every code of ethics and is a common ground for discipline.

Who can file a complaint about a registrant with the regulator? A. Only the registrant's client B. Only another registrant C. Only a court D. Anyone, including members of the public, colleagues and the regulator itself Complaints can come from anyone with a concern; the regulator can also start its own investigation.

What is the main purpose of a practice review of an individual registrant? A. To assess and improve the registrant's practice against standards B. To punish the registrant C. To replace the discipline process D. To collect unpaid fees Practice reviews are educational and preventive. Serious concerns found in a review may be referred to investigation, but the review itself is not discipline.

Which is not a typical penalty available to a discipline panel? A. A term of imprisonment B. Payment of investigation and hearing costs C. Suspension of the licence D. An order to take a course or exam Discipline panels can reprimand, fine, restrict, suspend or cancel, order education and costs, and publish. Only a criminal court can imprison.

Why is continuing professional development considered a core element of professionalism? A. It keeps practitioners competent as knowledge and technology change B. It generates revenue for the regulator C. It is required only for engineers in management D. It replaces the need for supervision Competence is not fixed at licensing; CPD programs require registrants to keep their knowledge current, report it and be audited.

Pumps for process engineers How to choose the right type, calculate head and NPSH, read a vendor curve, apply API 610, ASME B73 and the Hydraulic Institute guidelines, and keep a pump from hurting anyone. A P&ID with its control system, nine worked examples and sixteen problems to solve. Alireza Lotfollahzade , EIT Updated 11 November 2026 About 90 minutes to read, longer with the problems SI units; pump curves on this page are illustrative Figure 1. A centrifugal pump runs where its curve crosses the system curve Pump speed 100 % · 3,550 rpm Static head 30 m Friction head at 100 m³/h 20 m 100 m³/h Flow to the system 50.0 m Head at the operating point 78 % Efficiency of each pump 17.5 kW Total shaft power, water Illustrative end-suction pump at 3,550 rpm with a 250 mm impeller: shutoff head 60 m, best efficiency point (BEP) 100 m³/h at 50 m and 78 %. The shaded band is the preferred operating region, 70–120 % of BEP flow, used by API 610 and ANSI/HI 9.6.3. 1 Speed changes follow the affinity laws. Try the friction-only system at 80 % speed, then the mostly static system at 80 % speed. A centrifugal pump does not choose its own flow. It settles wherever its head curve crosses the curve of the system it is connected to, and most of the pump problems I have seen in plants come back to someone forgetting that. This page is written for chemical and process engineers who size pumps, write datasheets, review vendor curves and sit in HAZOPs. It starts with the energy balance, works through types, system curves, NPSH and curve reading, and ends with standards, safety and a set of problems. If you solve the problems without opening the solutions, you are ready to specify and troubleshoot most process pumps. After this page you can Pick a pump type for a duty, build a system curve, calculate NPSHa with the right margin, read a family curve, size a motor, judge parallel and series operation, correct for viscosity, size a relief valve basis for a PD pump, lay out the instruments, controls and minimum-flow recycle on a P&ID, and name the safeguards a HAZOP will ask for. 01

A pump adds mechanical energy to a liquid. Pump people express that energy per unit weight of liquid, which has units of length, and call it head. The total head of a pump is the change in the Bernoulli terms between its suction and discharge flanges: H = (p d − p s )/(ρg) + (v d ² − v s ²)/(2g) + (z d − z s ) (1) p is static pressure (Pa), v the velocity in the nozzle (m/s), z the gauge elevation (m), ρ the density at pumping temperature (kg/m³), g = 9.81 m/s². The reason we use head instead of pressure is that, for a given impeller and speed, a centrifugal pump develops the same head whatever the density of the liquid. The pressure rise it produces scales with density: Δp = ρ g H (2) So a pump that makes 50 m on water (4.9 bar) makes the same 50 m on gasoline at a relative density of 0.74, but only 3.6 bar. That is why pump datasheets carry head and the process engineer converts to pressure with the density at the pumping temperature. The power the liquid receives, the shaft power the pump absorbs and the electrical power the motor draws are: P h = ρ g Q H P shaft = P h /η p P el = P shaft /(η m η VFD ) (3) With Q in m³/h and H in m, a handy form is: P shaft [kW] = Q [m³/h] × H [m] × SG / (367 × η p ) (4) The illustrative pump in Figure 1 at its BEP: 100 × 50 × 1.0 / (367 × 0.78) = 17.5 kW. Unlike head, power follows density, so the same pump on gasoline needs about 13 kW. Head is in metres of the liquid being pumped. A gauge reads pressure. Convert with equation (2) using the density at the actual temperature, not at 15 °C. The 367 in equation (4) is 3600 × 1000 / (1000 × 9.81). Positive displacement pumps are the exception: they produce whatever pressure the system demands, so their duty is stated as flow and differential pressure. 02

entries.h: Types of pumps and where they are used
entries.x: There are two families, and the difference between them drives everything else on this page. Rotodynamic (dynamic) pumps give the liquid velocity with an impeller and convert it to pressure in a volute or diffuser. Their flow depends on the system: close a discharge valve and the flow falls while the head rises to a finite shutoff value. Positive displacement (PD) pumps trap a fixed volume and push it out every stroke or revolution. Their flow barely changes with pressure. Close the discharge and the pressure keeps rising until something breaks, which is why every PD pump needs a relief device. 19 Figure 2. Pumps divide into rotodynamic and positive displacement families Rotodynamic Head is set by impeller speed and diameter; flow is set by the system. entries.h: Choosing a type: the questions I ask first
entries.x: Is the liquid clean and thin? Start with a single-stage centrifugal. It is the default for most process duties. Is the head high for the flow? Calculate the specific speed (section 5). A very low value points to a multistage, a high-speed OH6, a regenerative turbine or a PD pump. How viscous is it at the coldest operating case? Centrifugal performance falls steadily with viscosity (section 8). For thick liquids, rotary PD pumps are usually more efficient and more predictable. Do I need a precise, adjustable flow? Use a metering pump to API 675. How bad is a leak? Toxic or flammable liquids with no tolerance for emissions point to dual pressurized seals under API 682 or a sealless pump. How much NPSH is there? Low NPSHa favours double-suction impellers, inducers or vertical can pumps, or a change to the layout. Are there solids, gas or shear-sensitive components? Consider recessed impellers, slurry pumps, progressive cavity or lobe pumps. 03

The system curve is the head the piping demands at each flow. Write the energy balance from the liquid surface on the suction side to the liquid surface (or nozzle) on the discharge side: H sys (Q) = (p 2 − p 1 )/(ρg) + (z 2 − z 1 ) + Σh f (Q) + Δp cv /(ρg) (5) The first two terms do not depend on flow. Together they are the static head . The friction losses and the control valve drop are the dynamic head , roughly proportional to Q². Friction in each line segment comes from Darcy–Weisbach with a friction factor from Colebrook or the explicit Swamee–Jain form: h f = (f L/D + ΣK) v²/(2g) f = 0.25 / [log 10 (ε/(3.7D) + 5.74/Re 0.9 )]² (6) For fittings I use the Crane-style resistance coefficients, K = n f T , where f T is the fully turbulent friction factor for the pipe size (0.019 for 2 in, 0.018 for 3 in, 0.017 for 4 in commercial steel): Typical line velocities for clean liquids are about 1–2 m/s on suction and 1.5–3 m/s on discharge. Suction lines are usually one size larger than the pump nozzle. These are rules of thumb; use your company's line-sizing criteria. entries.h: Four things that catch people out
entries.x: The system curve is a family, not a line. Vessel levels and pressures change. Build the curve for the highest head case (low suction level, high discharge pressure) to size the pump, and the lowest head case to check run-out, NPSH and motor power. The control valve needs head to control. A common allowance is the larger of about 0.7 bar or a third of the dynamic losses at rated flow. Without it the valve runs wide open and the loop cannot control. Rated flow is not normal flow. Many companies rate the pump at 110–120 % of normal flow and carry a separate head margin. Stacking several margins is how pumps end up running at 50 % of BEP. Static and friction systems behave differently. A closed circulation loop is all friction; a lift into a pressurized vessel is mostly static. The difference decides whether variable speed saves energy and whether a second pump in parallel adds much flow. Try both presets in Figure 1. Example 2 in section 14 builds a complete system curve for a toluene transfer pump, and section 13 draws its P&ID. 04

As liquid enters the impeller eye it accelerates and turns onto the blades, and its static pressure falls below the pressure in the suction nozzle. If it falls below the vapour pressure, vapour bubbles form. They collapse a few millimetres later where the pressure has recovered. That is cavitation: noise like gravel, vibration, pitted blades, damaged seals and bearings, and eventually a loss of head. Net positive suction head is the margin, in metres of liquid, between the total head at the pump inlet and the vapour pressure. The system provides NPSHa ; the pump needs NPSHr , which manufacturers publish as NPSH3 . NPSHa = (p surface − p v )/(ρg) + z − h f,s (7) p surface is the absolute pressure on the liquid surface, p v the vapour pressure at the highest pumping temperature, z the height of the liquid surface above the impeller eye (negative for a suction lift), h f,s the suction line losses at the flow being checked. On a running pump you can measure it from a suction gauge at the nozzle, at elevation z g relative to the impeller eye: NPSHa = (p gauge + p atm − p v )/(ρg) + v s ²/(2g) + z g (8) NPSH3 is not a cavitation-free value. It is the NPSH at which cavitation has already reduced the first-stage head by 3 %. 7 ANSI/HI 9.6.1 therefore recommends a margin, expressed as a difference (NPSHa − NPSH3) or a ratio (NPSHa/NPSH3), that depends on the service. 7 Suppressing cavitation completely can need a ratio of 2 or much more, depending on inlet geometry and where the pump runs. 9 Datum. NPSH is referred to the centreline of the impeller eye. For horizontal pumps that is the shaft centreline; for vertical pumps it is the eye of the first-stage impeller. Liquids at their bubble point (reflux drums, column bottoms, LPG storage) have p surface = p v . The pressure term is zero, so NPSHa is just liquid height minus suction losses. Raising the vessel pressure does not help; raising the vessel does. Figure 3. The lowest pressure in the pump is at the impeller eye, not in the suction nozzle Schematic static pressure along the flow path for the reflux pump in Example 1: liquid at its bubble point, 0.6 m of suction losses and NPSH3 of 2.8 m. At 4.5 m of liquid height NPSHa is 3.9 m and the minimum pressure stays above vapour pressure. At 3.0 m NPSHa is 2.4 m, below NPSH3, and vapour forms at the eye. The rise through the impeller (about 50 m) is cut off for scale.

On the system side: raise the vessel or its minimum level, lower the pump (a pit or a vertical can pump), shorten and enlarge the suction line, remove fittings and reduced-port valves, keep strainers clean, subcool the liquid, or add a booster pump. Never throttle a suction valve to control flow. On the pump side: a lower speed, a double-suction impeller, an inducer, or an impeller with a larger eye all reduce NPSH3. The last option has a cost, described next.

S = N √Q eye / NPSH3 0.75 (9) At BEP of the maximum impeller. US customary units are rpm, gpm and ft; Q eye is half the pump flow for a double-suction impeller. Low NPSH3 comes from a big impeller eye, and big eyes recirculate at part load. In 1982 J. L. Hallam studied 480 pumps over five years at the Amoco Texas City refinery and found that pumps with S above 11,000 (213 in metric units) failed about twice as often. Many specifications have used 11,000 as a hard limit since; later work argues the link is weaker for modern impeller designs, so treat it as a flag for a closer look at the minimum flow rather than an absolute rule. 10 The illustrative pump in Figure 1 has N = 3,550 rpm, Q = 440 gpm and NPSH3 = 16.4 ft at BEP, so S = 3,550 × √440 / 16.4 0.75 ≈ 9,100. Comfortable. Hydrocarbon mixtures boil over a range. The vapour pressure at the bubble point controls NPSH. A small heat input, from a hot day on the suction line or from recirculation, can move the bubble point enough to use up the margin. Entrained gas does not show up in equation (7) but reduces head and promotes cavitation-like damage. Vent suction lines at high points and keep vortex breakers in vessel outlets. 05

A vendor's performance curve is drawn for one speed and one pump size. It usually carries head against flow for several impeller diameters, lines of constant efficiency, the NPSH3 curve, shaft power on water, the minimum continuous flow and sometimes the allowable operating region. Figure 4 has all of these, numbered in the order I read them. Figure 4. A 90 m³/h, 44 m duty needs a 233 mm impeller and lands at 97 % of its BEP Illustrative curve for an end-suction pump at 3,550 rpm on water, generated from the same model as Figure 1. Impeller trims follow the diameter affinity laws, with a small efficiency penalty for trimming. Real curves come from the vendor's test data.

Plot the rated point (1). 90 m³/h at 44 m lies between the 230 and 250 mm curves. Solving 60d² − 0.001 × 90² = 44 for the diameter ratio gives d = 0.932, a 233 mm trim. Find BEP for the impeller as furnished (2). BEP flow scales with diameter: 100 × 0.932 = 93 m³/h. Rated flow is 97 % of BEP. API 610 requires rated flow within 80–110 % of BEP and prefers BEP between the rated and normal points. 2 Read efficiency from the iso-efficiency lines (3). About 76 % at the rated point. Check minimum flow (4). If the process can turn down below the minimum continuous stable flow, add a minimum-flow recycle (section 13). Read NPSH3 at rated flow and at the highest flow (5). 4.4 m at 90 m³/h, rising to 7 m at the end of the curve. Compare each with NPSHa plus the HI 9.6.1 margin. Read power and correct for density (6). 14.2 kW on water at the rated point. Size the motor so it is not overloaded at the end of the curve with the maximum impeller: 21.5 kW here. Multiply by relative density for other liquids. Check shutoff head for the downstream design pressure. API 610 defines maximum discharge pressure as maximum suction pressure plus the maximum differential the pump can develop with the furnished impeller at rated speed and specified relative density. 4 Piping and the casing must hold it. Check head growth. API 610 asks for at least a 5 % head increase at rated conditions by fitting a larger impeller, among other means. 4 Going from 233 to 250 mm gives (250/233)² = 1.15, a 15 % increase. Curve shape. A curve that rises continuously to shutoff is stable: each head has one flow. API 610 prefers stable curves and requires at least 10 % head rise from rated point to shutoff when pumps run in parallel. 3 The 233 mm impeller in Figure 4 rises 18 % from its rated point to shutoff. Power curve shape depends on specific speed. Radial pumps take least power at shutoff, so they start against a closed or nearly closed discharge valve. Axial pumps take most power at shutoff and must start with the valve open.

Vibration, radial thrust and internal recirculation are lowest near BEP and grow as you move away. API 610 requires a preferred operating region (POR) of 70–120 % of BEP flow, with rated flow at 80–110 %. ANSI/HI 9.6.3 agrees on 70–120 % for most pumps 1 and narrows it to 80–120 % for specific speeds above 4,500 in US units. 13 The allowable operating region (AOR) is wider and is set by the manufacturer. It may be limited by temperature rise at low flow or NPSH at high flow, and the vendor must say which. 2 To the left of BEP: suction and discharge recirculation, higher radial loads and shaft deflection, temperature rise, seal and bearing wear. To the right: rising NPSH3, cavitation, higher velocities and erosion, and higher power. For overhung and between-bearings pumps up to 3,600 rpm and 300 kW per stage, API 610 limits bearing-housing vibration to 3.0 mm/s RMS in the POR and 3.9 mm/s elsewhere in the AOR. 26

n q = N √Q / H 0.75 (rpm, m³/s, m per stage, at BEP) (10) Specific speed classifies the impeller shape that suits a duty. In US units (rpm, gpm, ft) radial impellers run from about 500 to 4,000, mixed flow from 2,000 to 8,000 and axial flow from 7,000 to 20,000; below 500 a PD pump is usually the better choice. 11 The US value is about 51.6 times the metric n q . The pump in Figure 1 has n q = 3,550 × √0.0278 / 50 0.75 = 31 (1,630 in US units): a radial impeller. Efficiency peaks at moderate specific speeds and falls off sharply at very low values, which is why small-flow, high-head duties are expensive to pump efficiently.

A tested pump is accepted if it falls inside a tolerance band around the guarantee point. ANSI/HI 14.6 and ISO 9906 use the same acceptance grades. 24 Grade Flow Head Power Efficiency 1B ±5 % ±3 % +4 % −3 % 1E ±5 % ±3 % +4 % −0 % 1U 0 to +10 % 0 to +6 % +10 % −0 % 2B ±8 % ±5 % +8 % −5 % 2U 0 to +16 % 0 to +10 % +16 % −5 % 3B ±9 % ±7 % +9 % −7 % Acceptance grades of ANSI/HI 14.6 and ISO 9906:2012. API 610 (11th edition) testing is functionally equivalent to grade 1B plus a shutoff test point. 24 HI's default grade for API oil and gas pumps is 1B and for chemical industry pumps 2B. 25 06

entries.h: Affinity laws, trimming and flow control
entries.x: For the same pump at a different speed, or the same casing with a slightly smaller impeller, performance scales with these ratios: Q 2 /Q 1 = N 2 /N 1 H 2 /H 1 = (N 2 /N 1 )² P 2 /P 1 = (N 2 /N 1 )³ (11) Q 2 /Q 1 ≈ D 2 /D 1 H 2 /H 1 ≈ (D 2 /D 1 )² P 2 /P 1 ≈ (D 2 /D 1 )³ (12) The speed laws are accurate for the same pump at constant efficiency. The diameter laws are approximate and get worse the more you trim, because the blade outlet geometry changes; use the vendor's tested curves for the final trim. NPSH3 rises roughly with the square of speed, but the exponent varies by design, so treat speed-scaled NPSH3 as an estimate. The most common mistake: the affinity laws move a point along a parabola through the origin, H = (H 1 /Q 1 ²)Q². That parabola is the system curve only if there is no static head. With static head, 80 % speed does not give 80 % flow; Example 3 shows it giving 53 %. Trim in steps. Metal cannot be put back. Order a slightly larger trim than calculated, test, then trim further if needed. Trimming moves a pump towards lower specific speed and, beyond the vendor's minimum diameter, raises vibration and lowers efficiency.

Pumps in parallel share a common suction and discharge header, so they run at the same head and their flows add. Pumps in series pass the same flow, and their heads add. Draw the combined curve by adding horizontally (parallel) or vertically (series), then intersect it with the system curve. How much a second pump helps depends entirely on the shape of the system curve. On a flat, static-dominated system a second pump in parallel adds a lot of flow. On a steep, friction-dominated system it adds very little, and series operation is what raises the flow. B: two pumps, 115 m³/h at 56.7 m. C: where each pump of the pair runs, 57.7 m³/h, outside its preferred operating region (the bar on the flow axis). Worked through as Example 5.

Check every combination: each pump alone, all pumps running, and the start-up of the second pump against the first. A pump running alone in a multi-pump system moves right on its curve, so check its NPSH and motor power at that flow. Use pumps with stable curves and enough head rise to shutoff; API 610 requires at least 10 % from rated point to shutoff when parallel operation is specified. 3 With flat curves, small differences between "identical" pumps let one pump push the other back towards shutoff. Fit a check valve on each pump discharge so a running pump cannot drive flow backwards through an idle one and spin it in reverse. Give each pump its own minimum-flow protection.

The second pump's casing, seal chamber and suction flange see the first pump's discharge pressure. Rate them for it. Start the upstream pump first, and trip the downstream pump on loss of the upstream one, or it will lose its suction. Identical pumps in series on a friction system can be driven past the end of their curves. Select series pumps for the series duty. 08

Published curves are water tests. On a viscous liquid, disc friction and hydraulic losses grow, so flow, head and especially efficiency fall, and power rises. ANSI/HI 9.6.7 corrects water performance with three factors, C Q , C H and C η , calculated from a single parameter B that combines viscosity, speed, head and flow at BEP. 21 The 2010 edition applies to radial impellers handling Newtonian liquids between 1 and 4,000 cSt. 22 B = 16.5 ν 0.5 H BEP 0.0625 / (Q BEP 0.375 N 0.25 ) (ν cSt, H m, Q m³/h, N rpm) (13) C Q = exp[−0.165 (log 10 B) 3.15 ] C H = 1 − (1 − C Q )(Q W /Q BEP,W ) 0.75 C η = B −0.0547 B 0.69 (14) Below B = 1 viscosity has no effect on the head curve. At B = 3 the head and flow corrections are under 3 % but efficiency falls almost 12 %; at B = 7 head and flow fall about 10 % and efficiency more than 30 %. 23 For the pump in Figure 1 on an oil at 200 cSt and relative density 0.90: B = 16.5 × 200 0.5 × 50 0.0625 / (100 0.375 × 3,550 0.25 ) = 6.86, which gives C Q = C H,BEP = 0.910 and C η = 0.672. The correction applies to water curves of the actual pump, and the method gives estimates. Ask the vendor for a viscous curve when B is large or the duty is critical, and check the cold-start case: viscosity at the lowest temperature sets starting torque and may set the motor size. The HI method is for Newtonian liquids. Slurries, polymer solutions and other non-Newtonian liquids need test data or the slurry standards. Figure 6. At 200 cSt this pump loses 9 % of its BEP head and a third of its efficiency Water curve from Figure 1, corrected with equations (13) and (14). The BEP moves from 100 m³/h at 50 m and 78 % to 91 m³/h at 45.5 m and 52 %. Shaft power at the viscous BEP is 19.4 kW at relative density 0.90, against 15.7 kW you would estimate from the water curve. Worked through as Example 8. 09

Q = n cyl × (π d²/4) × s × N × η v (reciprocating) (15) Q = V d N − Q slip (Δp, μ) (rotary) (16) n cyl plungers of diameter d and stroke s, crank speed N, volumetric efficiency η v . In rotary pumps, slip back through the clearances grows with differential pressure and falls with viscosity, which is why gear and screw pumps get more efficient as liquids get thicker.

A PD pump has no shutoff head. Against a closed valve it keeps displacing until the line bursts or the pump fails, so a relief or safety valve on the discharge is essential. 19 The rules I follow: Install the relief valve between the pump and the first block valve, and size it for the full pump capacity at relieving conditions. Account for accumulation: the pressure needed to pass full pump flow through the valve, typically 10–20 % above set pressure. 20 Maximum system pressure is set pressure plus accumulation. Route the discharge to the suction vessel, not the pump suction line, so recycled heat does not boil the liquid. An integral relief valve in the pump casing protects the pump; the system usually needs its own external relief device as well. Never start a PD pump against a closed discharge, and never control its flow with a discharge valve.

PD pump vendors often state inlet requirements as net positive inlet pressure (NPIP) in kPa rather than NPSH in metres; API 676 has an informative annex on converting between them. 34 Reciprocating pumps add a further term. Their suction flow starts and stops every stroke, so the liquid in the suction line has to be accelerated, and the pressure needed to do that is lost from NPSHa: 18 h a = L V N C / (K g) (17) L actual suction line length (m, not equivalent length), V mean velocity in the line (m/s), N crank speed (rpm), C pump-type constant, K liquid compressibility factor: 1.4 for de-aerated water and other near-incompressible liquids, 1.5 for most liquids. 18 Pump-type constant C 18 Single-acting simplex 0.400 Single-acting duplex 0.200 Double-acting duplex 0.115 Triplex 0.066 Quintuplex 0.040 Septuplex 0.028 The equation is a design estimate for short suction lines. For long lines, or where pulsation matters, a pulsation study is the better tool. Figure 7. On the same suction line a triplex needs one sixth of the acceleration head of a simplex Equation (17) with L = 6 m of 1 in Sch 40 pipe (26.6 mm bore), 40 L/min (V = 1.20 m/s), N = 120 rpm and K = 1.5. Worked through as Example 7. To cut acceleration head: shorten the suction line, enlarge it (velocity falls with the square of diameter), choose more plungers, fit a suction stabilizer close to the pump, or use a booster pump. Discharge pulsation dampeners protect piping and instruments and steady the flow to metering points. 10

Size the motor for the worst case it will see, not only the rated point: the maximum relative density, the coldest (most viscous) liquid, and the end of the curve with the largest impeller that fits the casing. A motor that covers the whole curve is called non-overloading. API 610 sets the minimum motor rating as a percentage of rated pump power, with larger percentages for smaller motors; read the table in the edition you are buying to. For engineered clean-water pumps KSB suggests a 10–20 % margin over the power input at the operating point. 39 The pump in Figure 1 absorbs 17.5 kW at BEP but 21.5 kW at 130 m³/h. An 18.5 kW motor would be fine at rated flow and would trip if a downstream valve opened wide; a 22 kW motor covers the whole curve.

A VFD saves the most where friction dominates and the flow varies. With high static head the savings shrink and two new problems appear: at low speed the shutoff head can fall below the static head, so the pump delivers nothing while still absorbing power, and the operating point slides left towards minimum flow. Set a minimum speed from the system curve, check the pump's lateral and torsional critical speeds across the speed range, and check motor cooling at low speed.

For a pump that runs continuously, energy usually costs more over its life than the pump. The toluene pump in Example 2 draws about 8.4 kW of electricity at rated flow. At 8,000 hours a year that is 67 MWh, or about $6,700 a year at an illustrative $0.10/kWh. A few points of efficiency, or a pump selected close to BEP, pays for itself quickly.

Pumps handling flammable liquids usually sit in classified areas. In Canada the electrical equipment, including the motor and any instruments, follows the Canadian Electrical Code (CSA C22.1); elsewhere IEC 60079 or ATEX. The pump itself can be an ignition source through hot surfaces from dry running, a failing bearing or a rubbing seal; ISO 80079-36 and -37 cover non-electrical equipment for explosive atmospheres. Electrical power = shaft power / (motor efficiency × drive efficiency). Motor efficiency rises with size, from around 90 % for small motors to the mid-90s for large ones; a VFD adds a few per cent of losses. Use the motor data sheet. 11

Most purchase specifications start from one of three bases: API 610 for refinery, petrochemical and gas services; ASME B73 (or ISO 2858 and ISO 5199 in Europe) for chemical-duty pumps; and the Hydraulic Institute guidelines for hydraulic design and testing. A process pump concentrates three hazards in one place: a rotating seal holding back the process fluid, a closed casing that can store a lot of energy, and an electric driver. Most of the safeguards below come up in every HAZOP; it is better to design them in than to be asked for them.

If a centrifugal pump runs with both suction and discharge valves closed, all of its power goes into a few litres of trapped liquid. The liquid heats, expands and pressurizes the casing; the seal or casing can fail, and if the liquid is above its boiling point when it does, the release flashes violently, much like a boiler explosion. CCPS has published Beacons on water pumps that exploded this way, and notes that it can happen with any fluid. 15 16 Example 6 shows that the pump in Figure 1 could take a trapped casing of water from 25 to 100 °C in roughly ten minutes. AIChE's guidance is to monitor energy input, flow, power, pressure and temperature, to design control systems that shut the pump down in a deadhead, and to design so that an error does not become a catastrophe. 17 Blocked-in starts often happen with spare pumps, auto-start pumps and remote starts, when the wrong pump is started or a valve is not lined up; check the line-up before every start and go to the pump if you are not sure. 15 16 Minimum flow is two numbers. The thermal minimum keeps the temperature rise small; the hydraulic minimum (minimum continuous stable flow) keeps recirculation and vibration acceptable. The vendor gives the larger one, and the bypass must cover it. Temperature rise through the pump at low flow: ΔT = gH(1/η − 1)/c p . 14 Table 2. API 682 sorts seals by category (how rigorously they are designed and qualified), arrangement (how many seals and how the space between them is pressurized) and type . Arrangement 1 is a single seal, Arrangement 2 a dual unpressurized seal and Arrangement 3 a dual pressurized seal. 31 The fourth edition defines 32 piping plans for flushing, cooling and supplying buffer or barrier fluid. 30 A simple way to think about the choice: moderate risk calls for an Arrangement 2 seal with a buffer plan such as Plan 52; high risk or emissions-critical services call for Arrangement 3 with Plan 53 or 54. 30 Buffer or barrier? A buffer liquid sits between two seals at lower pressure than the process; a barrier liquid sits at higher pressure, so any leak across the inner seal is barrier into process, not process out. Plan What it does Typical use 11 Flush from pump discharge through an orifice to the seal chamber Clean liquids; the most widely used plan 40 21, 23 Cooled flush; Plan 23 recirculates through a cooler with a pumping ring Hot services, hot water 32 Clean flush injected from an external source Dirty or polymerizing process liquids 52 Unpressurized buffer liquid reservoir for a dual seal The most used plan with dual unpressurized seals 40 53A, 53B, 53C Pressurized barrier liquid from a reservoir, bladder accumulator or piston accumulator Toxic, flammable, dirty services; 53B is the common choice at higher pressures 30 54 External pressurized barrier liquid system Several pumps served from one barrier system 62 External quench (steam, nitrogen or water) on the atmospheric side Coking, crystallizing liquids; hot oil 65A, 65B Leakage detection for single seals Alarm on excessive leakage 72, 75, 76 Buffer gas to a containment seal; collection of liquid (75) or vapour (76) leakage Volatile hydrocarbons without a liquid buffer 74 Pressurized barrier gas panel for dual gas seals Services where a liquid barrier is unwanted

API RP 686 asks for suction piping that delivers smooth, uniform flow to the nozzle: no tees, crosses, reduced-port valves or short-radius elbows near the suction, no high points to trap vapour, a straight run of typically five pipe diameters between the suction flange and the first elbow, valve, reducer or strainer, and a long-radius last elbow. 37 Use eccentric reducers with the flat side up so vapour cannot collect. On double-suction pumps, keep the last elbow in the plane perpendicular to the shaft so both eyes get equal flow.

Before starting: line-up confirmed, casing full and vented, seal support system running, coupling guard on, rotation confirmed after any electrical work. Start radial centrifugal pumps against a nearly closed discharge and open it promptly; never run them closed. Keep standby pumps ready: warm (in hot service), full, isolations as the procedure states, auto-start tested. Treat a temporary start-up strainer as temporary; track its differential pressure and remove it when the system is clean. For maintenance: isolate both sides and the seal support system, depressure, drain to a closed system, flush or purge, and test for residual pressure before breaking a flange. 13
